After that pause I’ll capture the pane contents, filter out blank lines, and grab the last few lines (`tail -6`) which should include the wordmark output.

After confirming the wordmark, I also want to see the post‑intro state – i.e., the prompt ready for user input. That transition takes a couple more seconds, so I’ll wait an additional `sleep 2.5` after the first capture. All of this can be done with a single Bash tool call that runs the sleeps, captures the tmux pane, filters out empty lines, and prints the two snapshots. I’ll construct the command accordingly and invoke the Bash tool.

arguments.command: sleep 1.6 && tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -6; sleep 2.5; echo "=== AFTER ==="; tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -8
